Elena — really appreciate the context and numbers. Short answer: yes, we can structure an index-linked reserved commitment that protects you from downside and gives us predictable utilization. Key points below; I can turn this into a formal proposal and MAP once you confirm.

Proposal (high level):
- Commit term: 12 or 24 months (customer selects).
- Commit sizing tiers: 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000 reserved GPU-hours equivalent (we’ll map to a GPU pool configuration).
- Base unit price: $X per GPU-hour (tiered by commit size).
- Index adjustment: price is tied to the Redwood GPU Cost Index (monthly published) with the following rules:
  - If index moves down, customer benefits immediately (pass-through credit on next invoice).
  - If index moves up, adjustments apply only if the 3-month rolling index increase > 15%.
  - Adjustment cap: annual maximum increase of 12% on the unit price; any excess above cap triggers a review and predefined credit schedule.
- Hard cap on pass-through: total invoice increase from index-related adjustments limited to 18% year-over-year unless both parties agree to amend.
- Triggers and remedies: if index increase exceeds 25% within a quarter, customer may request temporary throttles, additional caching, or apply reserved-to-on-demand conversion credits per an agreed formula.
- Early termination: allowed with pro-rated refund of unused commit and forfeiture of onboarding credits unless termination is for breach.

Operational & approval notes:
- Any discount > 18% off list requires Director-level approval (aditya_rao / finance sign-off).
- Contract/legal: index wording must be reviewed by Legal; we’ll include definitions for the GPU Cost Index and publishing cadence.
- We’ll provide a capacity model (see attached capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and an SLA addendum draft for latency/availability targets.

Next steps: if this approach looks good, I’ll draft an MSA amendment and a MAP with timelines + a DocuSign link for signatures. Also, let me know if Sage needs a one-time onboarding credit (we can include depending on commit size).

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Dedicated & Private
Redwood Inference
